22: There are two classes of spaces where bump functions are guaranteed to exist:
23: inner product spaces and finite-dimensional spaces.
24: 
25: In this file we define a typeclass `HasContDiffBump`
26: saying that a normed space has a family of smooth bump functions with certain properties.
27: 
28: We also define a structure `ContDiffBump` that holds the center and radii of the balls from above.
29: An element `f : ContDiffBump c` can be coerced to a function which is an infinitely smooth function
30: such that
31: 
32: - `f` is equal to `1` in `Metric.closedBall c f.rIn`;
33: - `support f = Metric.ball c f.rOut`;
34: - `0 ≤ f x ≤ 1` for all `x`.
35: 
36: ## Main Definitions
37: 
38: - `ContDiffBump (c : E)`: a structure holding data needed to construct
39:   an infinitely smooth bump function.
40: - `ContDiffBumpBase (E : Type*)`: a family of infinitely smooth bump functions
41:   that can be used to construct coercion of a `ContDiffBump (c : E)`
42:   to a function.
43: - `HasContDiffBump (E : Type*)`: a typeclass saying that `E` has a `ContDiffBumpBase`.
44:   Two instances of this typeclass (for inner product spaces and for finite-dimensional spaces)
45:   are provided elsewhere.
46: 
47: ## Keywords
48: 
49: smooth function, smooth bump function
50: -/

60: /-- `f : ContDiffBump c`, where `c` is a point in a normed vector space, is a
61: bundled smooth function such that
62: 
63: - `f` is equal to `1` in `Metric.closedBall c f.rIn`;
64: - `support f = Metric.ball c f.rOut`;
65: - `0 ≤ f x ≤ 1` for all `x`.
66: 
67: The structure `ContDiffBump` contains the data required to construct the function:
68: real numbers `rIn`, `rOut`, and proofs of `0 < rIn < rOut`. The function itself is available through
69: `CoeFun` when the space is nice enough, i.e., satisfies the `HasContDiffBump` typeclass. -/
70: structure ContDiffBump (c : E) where
71:   /-- real numbers `0 < rIn < rOut` -/
72:   (rIn rOut : ℝ)
73:   rIn_pos : 0 < rIn
74:   rIn_lt_rOut : rIn < rOut
75: 
76: /-- The base function from which one will construct a family of bump functions. One could
77: add more properties if they are useful and satisfied in the examples of inner product spaces
78: and finite-dimensional vector spaces, notably derivative norm control in terms of `R - 1`.

80: TODO: do we ever need `f x = 1 ↔ ‖x‖ ≤ 1`? -/
81: structure ContDiffBumpBase (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] where
82:   /-- The function underlying this family of bump functions -/
83:   toFun : ℝ → E → ℝ
84:   mem_Icc : ∀ (R : ℝ) (x : E), toFun R x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1

86:   smooth : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (uncurry toFun) (Ioi (1 : ℝ) ×ˢ (univ : Set E))
87:   eq_one : ∀ R : ℝ, 1 < R → ∀ x : E, ‖x‖ ≤ 1 → toFun R x = 1
88:   support : ∀ R : ℝ, 1 < R → Function.support (toFun R) = Metric.ball (0 : E) R

90: /-- A class registering that a real vector space admits bump functions. This will be instantiated
91: first for inner product spaces, and then for finite-dimensional normed spaces.
92: We use a specific class instead of `Nonempty (ContDiffBumpBase E)` for performance reasons. -/
93: class HasContDiffBump (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] : Prop where
94:   out : Nonempty (ContDiffBumpBase E)

96: /-- In a space with `C^∞` bump functions, register some function that will be used as a basis
97: to construct bump functions of arbitrary size around any point. -/
98: def someContDiffBumpBase (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
99:     [hb : HasContDiffBump E] : ContDiffBumpBase E :=
100:   Nonempty.some hb.out

104: theorem rOut_pos {c : E} (f : ContDiffBump c) : 0 < f.rOut :=

111: instance (c : E) : Inhabited (ContDiffBump c) :=

13: # Smooth bump functions in inner product spaces
14: 
15: In this file we prove that a real inner product space has smooth bump functions,
16: see `hasContDiffBump_of_innerProductSpace`.
17: 
18: ## Keywords
19: 
20: smooth function, bump function, inner product space

30: /-- A base bump function in an inner product space. This construction works in any space with a
31: norm smooth away from zero but we do not have a typeclass for this. -/
32: noncomputable def ContDiffBumpBase.ofInnerProductSpace : ContDiffBumpBase E where
33:   toFun R x := smoothTransition ((R - ‖x‖) / (R - 1))
34:   mem_Icc _ _ := ⟨smoothTransition.nonneg _, smoothTransition.le_one _⟩
35:   symmetric _ _ := by simp only [norm_neg]
36:   smooth := by
37:     rintro ⟨R, x⟩ ⟨hR : 1 < R, -⟩
38:     apply ContDiffAt.contDiffWithinAt
39:     rw [← sub_pos] at hR
40:     rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx
41:     · have A : ContinuousAt (fun p : ℝ × E ↦ (p.1 - ‖p.2‖) / (p.1 - 1)) (R, 0) := by
42:         fun_prop (disch := positivity)
43:       have B : ∀ᶠ p in 𝓝 (R, (0 : E)), 1 ≤ (p.1 - ‖p.2‖) / (p.1 - 1) :=
44:         A.eventually <| le_mem_nhds <| (one_lt_div hR).2 <| sub_lt_sub_left (by simp) _
45:       refine (contDiffAt_const (c := 1)).congr_of_eventuallyEq <| B.mono fun _ ↦
46:         smoothTransition.one_of_one_le
47:     · refine smoothTransition.contDiffAt.comp _ (ContDiffAt.div ?_ (by fun_prop) hR.ne')
48:       exact contDiffAt_fst.sub (contDiffAt_snd.norm ℝ hx)
49:   eq_one _ hR _ hx := smoothTransition.one_of_one_le <| (one_le_div <| sub_pos.2 hR).2 <|
50:     sub_le_sub_left hx _
51:   support R hR := by
52:     ext x
53:     rw [mem_support, Ne, smoothTransition.zero_iff_nonpos, not_le, mem_ball_zero_iff]
54:     simp [hR]
55: 
56: /-- Any inner product space has smooth bump functions. -/
57: instance (priority := 100) hasContDiffBump_of_innerProductSpace : HasContDiffBump E :=
58:   ⟨⟨.ofInnerProductSpace E⟩⟩

11: /-!
12: # Functions which vanish as distributions vanish as functions
13: 
14: In a finite-dimensional normed real vector space endowed with a Borel measure, consider a locally
15: integrable function whose integral against all compactly supported smooth functions vanishes. Then
16: the function is almost everywhere zero.
17: This is proved in `ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero`.
18: 
19: A version for two functions having the same integral when multiplied by smooth compactly supported
20: functions is also given in `ae_eq_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq`.
21: 
22: These are deduced from the same results on finite-dimensional real manifolds, given respectively
23: as `ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contMDiff_smul_eq_zero` and `ae_eq_of_integral_contMDiff_smul_eq`.
24: -/

42: /-- If a locally integrable function `f` on a finite-dimensional real manifold has zero integral
43: when multiplied by any smooth compactly supported function, then `f` vanishes almost everywhere. -/
44: theorem ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contMDiff_smul_eq_zero [SigmaCompactSpace M]
45:     (hf : LocallyIntegrable f μ)
46:     (h : ∀ g : M → ℝ, CMDiff ∞ g → HasCompactSupport g → ∫ x, g x • f x ∂μ = 0) :
47:     ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, f x = 0 := by
48:   -- record topological properties of `M`
49:   have := I.locallyCompactSpace
50:   have := ChartedSpace.locallyCompactSpace H M
51:   have := I.secondCountableTopology
52:   have := ChartedSpace.secondCountable_of_sigmaCompact H M
53:   let _ : MetricSpace M := TopologicalSpace.metrizableSpaceMetric M
54:   -- it suffices to show that the integral of the function vanishes on any compact set `s`
55:   apply ae_eq_zero_of_forall_setIntegral_isCompact_eq_zero' hf (fun s hs ↦ Eq.symm ?_)
56:   obtain ⟨δ, δpos, hδ⟩ : ∃ δ, 0 < δ ∧ IsCompact (cthickening δ s) := hs.exists_isCompact_cthickening
57:   -- choose a sequence of smooth functions `gₙ` equal to `1` on `s` and vanishing outside of the
58:   -- `uₙ`-neighborhood of `s`, where `uₙ` tends to zero. Then each integral `∫ gₙ f` vanishes,
59:   -- and by dominated convergence these integrals converge to `∫ x in s, f`.
60:   obtain ⟨u, -, u_pos, u_lim⟩ : ∃ u, StrictAnti u ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ), u n ∈ Ioo 0 δ)
61:     ∧ Tendsto u atTop (𝓝 0) := exists_seq_strictAnti_tendsto' δpos
62:   let v : ℕ → Set M := fun n ↦ thickening (u n) s
63:   obtain ⟨K, K_compact, vK⟩ : ∃ K, IsCompact K ∧ ∀ n, v n ⊆ K :=
64:     ⟨_, hδ, fun n ↦ thickening_subset_cthickening_of_le (u_pos n).2.le _⟩
65:   have : ∀ n, ∃ (g : M → ℝ), support g = v n ∧ CMDiff ∞ g ∧ Set.range g ⊆ Set.Icc 0 1
66:           ∧ ∀ x ∈ s, g x = 1 := by
67:     intro n
68:     rcases exists_contMDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff I isOpen_thickening hs.isClosed
69:       (self_subset_thickening (u_pos n).1 s) with ⟨g, g_smooth, g_range, g_supp, hg⟩
70:     exact ⟨g, g_supp, g_smooth, g_range, fun x hx ↦ (hg x).1 hx⟩
71:   choose g g_supp g_diff g_range hg using this
72:   -- main fact: the integral of `∫ gₙ f` tends to `∫ x in s, f`.
73:   have L : Tendsto (fun n ↦ ∫ x, g n x • f x ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x in s, f x ∂μ)) := by
74:     rw [← integral_indicator hs.measurableSet]
75:     let bound : M → ℝ := K.indicator (fun x ↦ ‖f x‖)
76:     have A : ∀ n, AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x ↦ g n x • f x) μ :=
77:       fun n ↦ (g_diff n).continuous.aestronglyMeasurable.smul hf.aestronglyMeasurable
78:     have B : Integrable bound μ := by
79:       rw [integrable_indicator_iff K_compact.measurableSet]
80:       exact (hf.integrableOn_isCompact K_compact).norm
81:     have C : ∀ n, ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ‖g n x • f x‖ ≤ bound x := by
82:       intro n
83:       filter_upwards with x
84:       rw [norm_smul]
85:       refine le_indicator_apply (fun _ ↦ ?_) (fun hxK ↦ ?_)
86:       · have : ‖g n x‖ ≤ 1 := by
87:           have := g_range n (mem_range_self (f := g n) x)
88:           rw [Real.norm_of_nonneg this.1]
89:           exact this.2
90:         exact mul_le_of_le_one_left (norm_nonneg _) this
91:       · have : g n x = 0 := by rw [← notMem_support, g_supp]; contrapose hxK; exact vK n hxK
92:         simp [this]
93:     have D : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => g n x • f x) atTop (𝓝 (s.indicator f x)) := by
94:       filter_upwards with x
95:       by_cases hxs : x ∈ s
96:       · have : ∀ n, g n x = 1 := fun n ↦ hg n x hxs
97:         simp [this, indicator_of_mem hxs f]
98:       · simp_rw [indicator_of_notMem hxs f]
99:         apply tendsto_const_nhds.congr'
100:         suffices H : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, g n x = 0 by
101:           filter_upwards [H] with n hn using by simp [hn]
102:         obtain ⟨ε, εpos, hε⟩ : ∃ ε, 0 < ε ∧ x ∉ thickening ε s := by
103:           rw [← hs.isClosed.closure_eq, closure_eq_iInter_thickening s] at hxs
104:           simpa using hxs
105:         filter_upwards [(tendsto_order.1 u_lim).2 _ εpos] with n hn
106:         rw [← notMem_support, g_supp]
107:         contrapose hε
108:         exact thickening_mono hn.le s hε
109:     exact tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence bound A B C D
110:   -- deduce that `∫ x in s, f = 0` as each integral `∫ gₙ f` vanishes by assumption
111:   have : ∀ n, ∫ x, g n x • f x ∂μ = 0 := by
112:     refine fun n ↦ h _ (g_diff n) ?_
113:     apply HasCompactSupport.of_support_subset_isCompact K_compact
114:     simpa [g_supp] using vK n
115:   simpa [this] using L

87: /-- A version of `fundamental_theorem_of_variational_calculus'` for `Continuous f`.
88: The proof uses assumption that source of `f` is finite-dimensional
89: inner-product space, so that a bump function with compact support exists via
90: `ContDiffBump.hasCompactSupport` from `Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.Basic`.
91: 
92: The proof is by contradiction, assume that there is `x₀` such that `f x₀ ≠ 0` then one construct
93: construct `g` test function *supported* on the neighborhood of `x₀` such that `⟪f x, g x⟫ ≥ 0`
94: and `⟪f x, g x⟫ > 0` on a neighborhood of x₀.
95: 
96: Using `Y` for the theorem below to make use of bump functions in InnerProductSpaces. `Y` is
97: a finite dimensional measurable space over `ℝ` with (standard) inner product.

101:     [OpensMeasurableSpace Y]

112:     let x₂ := f₂ x₀
113:   -- x₂ ≠ 0 because `fromL2 (toL2 (f x₀)) = f x₀`

127:       intros x hx
128:     -- hx : x ∈ ball x₀ δ₂, so dist x x₀ < δ₂, hence
129:     -- this is |⟪u,v⟫| ≤ ‖u‖ * ‖v‖, in the genuine InnerProductSpace on WithLp 2 V

14: In this module we define the type class `InnerProductSpace' 𝕜 E` which is a

17: Instead `E` is equipped with a L₂ norm `‖x‖₂` which satisfies `‖x‖₂ = √⟪x,x⟫`.
18:

20: pi types `ι → E`, which would otherwise not be possible due to the use of max norm on these types.
21: 
22: We define the following maps:

24: - `InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E → InnerProductSpace' 𝕜 E` which sets `‖x‖₂ = ‖x‖`.
25: - `InnerProductSpace' 𝕜 E → InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (WithLp 2 E)` which uses the fact that the norm

121: In the definition of an inner product space, we require the existence of a norm, which is equal
122: (but maybe not defeq) to the square root of the scalar product. This makes it possible to put
123: an inner product space structure on spaces with a preexisting norm (for instance `ℝ`), with good
124: properties. However, sometimes, one would like to define the norm starting only from a well-behaved
125: scalar product. This is what we implement in this paragraph, starting from a structure
126: `InnerProductSpace.Core` stating that we have a nice scalar product.
127: 
128: Our goal here is not to develop a whole theory with all the supporting API, as this will be done
129: below for `InnerProductSpace`. Instead, we implement the bare minimum to go as directly as
130: possible to the construction of the norm and the proof of the triangular inequality.
131: 
132: Warning: Do not use this `Core` structure if the space you are interested in already has a norm
133: instance defined on it, otherwise this will create a second non-defeq norm instance!
134: -/
135: 
136: /-- A structure requiring that a scalar product is positive semidefinite and symmetric. -/
137: structure PreInnerProductSpace.Core (𝕜 : Type*) (F : Type*) [RCLike 𝕜] [AddCommGroup F]
138:     [Module 𝕜 F] extends Inner 𝕜 F where
139:   /-- The inner product is *Hermitian*, taking the `conj` swaps the arguments. -/
140:   conj_inner_symm x y : conj (inner y x) = inner x y
141:   /-- The inner product is positive (semi)definite. -/
142:   re_inner_nonneg x : 0 ≤ re (inner x x)
143:   /-- The inner product is additive in the first coordinate. -/
144:   add_left x y z : inner (x + y) z = inner x z + inner y z
145:   /-- The inner product is conjugate linear in the first coordinate. -/
146:   smul_left x y r : inner (r • x) y = conj r * inner x y
147: 
148: attribute [class] PreInnerProductSpace.Core
149: 
150: /-- A structure requiring that a scalar product is positive definite. Some theorems that
151: require these assumptions are put under section `InnerProductSpace.Core`. -/
152: structure InnerProductSpace.Core (𝕜 : Type*) (F : Type*) [RCLike 𝕜] [AddCommGroup F]
153:   [Module 𝕜 F] extends PreInnerProductSpace.Core 𝕜 F where
154:   /-- The inner product is positive definite. -/
155:   definite : ∀ x, inner x x = 0 → x = 0

93: construct `g` test function *supported* on the neighborhood of `x₀` such that `⟪f x, g x⟫ ≥ 0`
94: and `⟪f x, g x⟫ > 0` on a neighborhood of x₀.

97: a finite dimensional measurable space over `ℝ` with (standard) inner product.

116:   -- continuity of f₂ at x₀

179:     have support_subset : Function.support φ ⊆ Metric.ball x₀ δ₂ :=
180:       hφ_support_subset.trans (Metric.ball_subset_ball (by linarith))
181:     have supp_subset2 : Function.support (fun x => φ x * ⟪f x, f x₀⟫_ℝ) ⊆ Function.support φ := by
182:       intro x hprod hφ0
183:     -- if φ x = 0 then φ x * inner = 0, contradiction
184:       simp [hφ0] at hprod
185:     have hinner_cont : Continuous (fun x => ⟪f x, f x₀⟫_ℝ) :=
186:       Continuous.inner' (f : Y → V) (fun _ => f x₀) hf continuous_const
187:     have integrable_prod :
188:       Integrable (fun x => φ x * ⟪f x, f x₀⟫_ℝ) μ :=
189:     -- (i) build a `HasCompactSupport` witness for the product
190:       (Continuous.mul hφ_testfun.smooth.continuous hinner_cont).integrable_of_hasCompactSupport
191:         (hφ_testfun.supp.mono supp_subset2)
192: 
193:   -- [4.2.2] Nonnegativity everywhere (`h_nonneg`)
194:     have h_nonneg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ φ x * ⟪f x, f x₀⟫_ℝ := by
195:       intro x
196:       by_cases hx : x ∈ Function.support φ
197:       · -- on the support, φ ≥ 0 and ⟪f x, f x₀⟫ > 0
198:         exact mul_nonneg (hφ_non_neg x hx) (inner_pos_V x (support_subset hx)).le
199:       · -- off the support, φ x = 0 so the product is 0
200:         simp [Function.notMem_support.mp hx]
201: 
202:   -- [4.2.3] That closed ball has positive measure, and is contained in the support
203:     -- every nonempty open set has positive measure
204:     have hμ_ball : 0 < μ (Metric.ball x₀ (δ₂/4)) :=
205:       Metric.isOpen_ball.measure_pos μ (Metric.nonempty_ball.mpr (by linarith))
206:     have hμ : 0 < μ (Metric.closedBall x₀ (δ₂/4)) :=
207:       lt_of_lt_of_le hμ_ball (measure_mono Metric.ball_subset_closedBall)
208:     have closedBall_subset_support :
209:         Metric.closedBall x₀ (δ₂/4)
210:           ⊆ Function.support (fun x => φ x * ⟪f x, f x₀⟫_ℝ) := by
211:         intro x hx
212:         have hφx := hφ_pos_inner x hx
213:         have hin : 0 < ⟪f x, f x₀⟫_ℝ :=
214:           inner_pos_V x (Metric.closedBall_subset_ball (by linarith) hx)
215:         simp only [Function.support_mul, Set.mem_inter_iff, Function.mem_support, ne_eq]
216:         constructor
217:         · linarith
218:         · linarith
219: 
220:   -- [4.2.4] putting everything together: positivity contradicts `key_integral : ∫ ... = 0`
221:     have integral_pos : 0 < ∫ x, φ x * ⟪f x, f x₀⟫_ℝ ∂μ :=
222:       (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg h_nonneg integrable_prod).mpr
223:         (lt_of_lt_of_le hμ (measure_mono closedBall_subset_support))
224:     linarith

46:     ∃ f : E → ℝ,
47:       tsupport f ⊆ s ∧ HasCompactSupport f ∧ ContDiff ℝ n f ∧ range f ⊆ Icc 0 1 ∧ f x = 1 := by
48:   obtain ⟨d : ℝ, d_pos : 0 < d, hd : Euclidean.closedBall x d ⊆ s⟩ :=

50:   let c : ContDiffBump (toEuclidean x) :=
51:     { rIn := d / 2
52:       rOut := d
53:       rIn_pos := half_pos d_pos

12: # Inner product space
13: 
14: In this module we define the type class `InnerProductSpace' 𝕜 E` which is a
15: generalization of `InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E`, as it does not require the condition `‖x‖^2 = ⟪x,x⟫`
16: but instead the condition `∃ (c > 0) (d > 0), c • ‖x‖^2 ≤ ⟪x,x⟫ ≤ d • ‖x‖^2`.
17: Instead `E` is equipped with a L₂ norm `‖x‖₂` which satisfies `‖x‖₂ = √⟪x,x⟫`.
18: 
19: This allows us to define the inner product space structure on product types `E × F` and
20: pi types `ι → E`, which would otherwise not be possible due to the use of max norm on these types.
21: 
22: We define the following maps:
23: 
24: - `InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E → InnerProductSpace' 𝕜 E` which sets `‖x‖₂ = ‖x‖`.
25: - `InnerProductSpace' 𝕜 E → InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (WithLp 2 E)` which uses the fact that the norm
26:   defined on `WithLp 2 E` is L₂ norm.
27: 
28: -/
29: 
30: @[expose] public section
31: 
32: /-- L₂ norm on `E`.
33: 
34: In particular, on product types `X×Y` and pi types `ι → X` this class provides L₂ norm unlike `‖·‖`.
35: -/
36: class Norm₂ (E : Type*) where
37:   norm₂ : E → ℝ
38: 
39: export Norm₂ (norm₂)
40: 
41: attribute [inherit_doc Norm₂] norm₂
42: 
43: @[inherit_doc Norm₂]
44: notation:max "‖" x "‖₂" => norm₂ x
45: 
46: open RCLike ComplexConjugate
47: 
48: /-- Effectively as `InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E` but it does not requires that `‖x‖^2 = ⟪x,x⟫`. It is
49: only required that they are equivalent `∃ (c > 0) (d > 0), c • ‖x‖^2 ≤ ⟪x,x⟫ ≤ d • ‖x‖^2`. The main
50: purpose of this class is to provide inner product space structure on product types `ExF` and
51: pi types `ι → E` without using `WithLp` gadget.
52: 
53: If you want to access L₂ norm use `‖x‖₂ := √⟪x,x⟫`.
54: 
55: This class induces `InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (WithLp 2 E)` which equips `‖·‖` on `X` with L₂ norm.
56: This is very useful when translating results from `InnerProductSpace` to `InnerProductSpace'`
57: together with `toL2 : E →L[𝕜] (WithLp 2 E)` and `fromL2 : (WithL2 2 E) →L[𝕜] E`.
58: 
59: In short we have these implications:
60: ```
61:   InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E → InnerProductSpace' 𝕜 E
62:   InnerProductSpace' 𝕜 E → InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (WithLp 2 E)
63: ```
64: 
65: The reason behind this type class is that with current mathlib design the requirement
66: `‖x‖^2 = ⟪x,x⟫` prevents us to give inner product space structure on product type `E×F` and pi
67: type `ι → E` as they are equipped with max norm. One has to work with `WithLp 2 (E×F)` and
68: `WithLp 2 (ι → E)`. This places quite a bit inconvenience on users in certain scenarios.
69: In particular, the main motivation behind this class is to make computations of `adjFDeriv` and
70: `gradient` easy.
71: -/
72: class InnerProductSpace' (𝕜 : Type*) (E : Type*) [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
73:     extends Norm₂ E where
74:   /-- Core inner product properties. -/
75:   core : InnerProductSpace.Core 𝕜 E
76:   /-- The inner product induces the L₂ norm. -/
77:   norm₂_sq_eq_re_inner : ∀ x : E, ‖x‖₂ ^ 2 = re (core.inner x x)
78:   /-- Norm induced by inner product is topologically equivalent to the given norm on E. -/
79:   inner_top_equiv_norm : ∃ c d : ℝ,

81:     ∀ x : E, (c • ‖x‖^2 ≤ re (core.inner x x)) ∧ (re (core.inner x x) ≤ d • ‖x‖^2)

30: /-- A base bump function in an inner product space. This construction works in any space with a
31: norm smooth away from zero but we do not have a typeclass for this. -/
32: noncomputable def ContDiffBumpBase.ofInnerProductSpace : ContDiffBumpBase E where
33:   toFun R x := smoothTransition ((R - ‖x‖) / (R - 1))
34:   mem_Icc _ _ := ⟨smoothTransition.nonneg _, smoothTransition.le_one _⟩
35:   symmetric _ _ := by simp only [norm_neg]
36:   smooth := by
37:     rintro ⟨R, x⟩ ⟨hR : 1 < R, -⟩
38:     apply ContDiffAt.contDiffWithinAt
39:     rw [← sub_pos] at hR
40:     rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx
41:     · have A : ContinuousAt (fun p : ℝ × E ↦ (p.1 - ‖p.2‖) / (p.1 - 1)) (R, 0) := by
42:         fun_prop (disch := positivity)
43:       have B : ∀ᶠ p in 𝓝 (R, (0 : E)), 1 ≤ (p.1 - ‖p.2‖) / (p.1 - 1) :=
44:         A.eventually <| le_mem_nhds <| (one_lt_div hR).2 <| sub_lt_sub_left (by simp) _
45:       refine (contDiffAt_const (c := 1)).congr_of_eventuallyEq <| B.mono fun _ ↦
46:         smoothTransition.one_of_one_le
47:     · refine smoothTransition.contDiffAt.comp _ (ContDiffAt.div ?_ (by fun_prop) hR.ne')
48:       exact contDiffAt_fst.sub (contDiffAt_snd.norm ℝ hx)
49:   eq_one _ hR _ hx := smoothTransition.one_of_one_le <| (one_le_div <| sub_pos.2 hR).2 <|
50:     sub_le_sub_left hx _

53:     rw [mem_support, Ne, smoothTransition.zero_iff_nonpos, not_le, mem_ball_zero_iff]
54:     simp [hR]
